clue.text: One cause of those monster headlines?

definitions.text: One cause of those monster headlines?

parts.words: One cause of those monster headlines?
parts.note: the huge type of a tabloid front page is blamed on a style of journalism that goes for shock and excitement

explanation.surface: A question about what lies behind giant newspaper headlines.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid, exaggerated reporting meant to excite readers is what produces screaming banner headlines.

clue.text: Makes oneself cheap? Just the opposite

definitions.text: Makes oneself cheap? Just the opposite

parts.words: Makes oneself cheap? Just the opposite
parts.note: the opposite of cheap is dear, so this is making oneself dear, that is beloved

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of lowering themselves, and the reply is that they do the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: To win affection is to make oneself dear to people, and dear is the opposite of cheap.

clue.text: A medium state maybe:

parts.note: a spiritualist medium is said to go into a dazed condition when contacting the dead

explanation.surface: A remark about some middling condition.
explanation.definitionFit: A séance medium supposedly enters a hypnotic, dreamlike state to receive spirit messages.

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual abbreviation for a sailor
aft means at or towards the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A sailor is at the back of the ship, along with everything else trailing behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Abaft is a nautical word for towards the stern, i.e. behind.

clue.text: On receipt of which one deals with the pack

definitions.text: On receipt of which one deals with the pack

parts.words: On receipt of which one deals with the pack
parts.note: pretends to be about dealing cards from a pack, but means packing one's bags after being dismissed

explanation.surface: Someone is handed something and starts dealing out a pack of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a card game; 'deals with the pack' really means packs up to leave after being told to go.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sent packing, a dismissed person receives a notice of departure and gets their kit together.

clue.text: Scream due to gin — this could prove a damper

indicators.note: the letters of the first four words could prove, when rearranged, to be another word

explanation.surface: A scream brought on by gin might put a damper on the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could prove' signals that the fourteen letters of 'Scream due to gin' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that disheartens people acts as a damper on their spirits.

clue.text: "Far-off Ind"? Not to the Detrotiter

parts.note: the poetic far-off Ind is India, but for someone from Detroit the similar-sounding US state is just next door

explanation.surface: A quotation about distant India, which someone from Detroit would not find distant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detrotiter' is an OCR slip for Detroiter, a person from Detroit, Michigan, which borders this state.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the US state resembles India with an extra syllable, and it neighbours Michigan.

clue.text: "His heart was one of those which most us," (Byron)

definitions.text: "His heart was one of those which most us," (Byron)

parts.words: "His heart was one of those which most us," (Byron)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Byron: the missing verb means to charm or captivate

explanation.surface: A line of Byron with a word left out.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing verb means to make someone fall in love, fitting a heart that charms.

clue.text: Cheat's make-up could put one wise'

indicators.note: the make-up of a word is its letters, here rearranged into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A cheat's disguise could fool even a sage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' looks like a cheat's disguise, but signals rearranging the five letters of 'Cheat's'.
explanation.definitionFit: To instruct someone is to put them wise, giving them knowledge.

clue.text: Dismount during the joust

parts.note: a knight knocked off his horse in a tournament is thrown from the saddle

explanation.surface: A knight comes off his horse in the middle of a tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw a rider from the saddle is the jousting goal of removing him from his place.

clue.text: "Breakfast, supper, dinner, ——" (Bring).

parts.note: a list of meals with one missing: the midday meal completes the set

explanation.surface: A quoted list of meals with the last one blanked out.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is the formal name for the midday meal, alongside the other meals listed.

clue.text: Near crock, possibly, getting the bird

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of the two words could be ordered another way

explanation.surface: A nearly broken-down old wreck gets jeered at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting the bird' suggests being booed; here 'the bird' is the definition and 'possibly' rearranges NEAR CROCK.
explanation.definitionFit: The corncrake is a secretive rail of grassland, a bird known for its rasping call.

clue.text: Even a most skilful artiste may show virus too!

indicators.note: may show suggests the letters of the two words can show a different word when rearranged

explanation.surface: Even the greatest performer can fall ill with a virus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may show' rearranges the eight letters of VIRUS TOO.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer of exceptional technical brilliance, especially a musician, is a master of their art.

clue.text: Hard to get far down into this

definitions.text: Hard to get far down into this

parts.words: Hard to get far down into this
parts.note: refers to a prank bed whose sheet is folded so the sleeper cannot stretch their legs out

explanation.surface: Something that is difficult to penetrate deeply.
explanation.walkthrough: An apple-pie bed is a schoolboy prank: the bottom sheet is folded back so the victim's feet stop halfway down.
explanation.definitionFit: The prank bed is made so the victim's legs are blocked halfway down the sheets.

clue.text: Master, piper, or so we hope

definitions.text: Master, piper, or so we hope

parts.words: Master, piper, or so we hope
parts.note: a tradesman we hope is a master of his craft and who works on pipes

explanation.surface: A list praising someone as a master and a piper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piper' suggests a bagpipe player; here it is someone who works with water pipes, and a master tradesman is hoped for.
explanation.definitionFit: This tradesman fits and mends water pipes; 'master' is a qualified rank in the trade.

clue.text: She was temporarily taken in by a bit of an ass!

definitions.text: She was temporarily taken in by a bit of an ass!

parts.words: She was temporarily taken in by a bit of an ass!
parts.note: in A Midsummer Night's Dream the fairy queen, under a love spell, dotes on Bottom wearing a donkey's head

explanation.surface: A woman was briefly fooled by a silly man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of an ass' sounds like a fool, but Bottom literally had an ass's head in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Queen of the Fairies is bewitched into loving the ass-headed weaver Bottom.

clue.text: Homely apple-coloured dress?

parts.note: the word is a variety of apple, a reddish-brown colour and a coarse homespun cloth

explanation.surface: A plain frock in an apple shade.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a rough country cloth, the reddish-brown colour and a rough-skinned apple variety.

clue.text: Short, but not always sweet, so to speak

definitions.text: Short, but not always sweet, so to speak

parts.words: Short, but not always sweet, so to speak
parts.note: plays on the phrase short and sweet: brief speech that is not always kind

explanation.surface: A comment that brevity is not always pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Curt, abrupt speech is brief but can come across as unfriendly.

clue.text: Like 'someone having: suffered capital loss

parts.note: capital loss sounds financial but means losing one's head, being cut short at the top

explanation.surface: A person who has lost money on investments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests money; here it is the head (Latin caput), so the person is cut off at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cut short by having its top or end chopped off has been shortened.

clue.text: A hold-up in passing the port

definitions.text: A hold-up in passing the port

parts.words: A hold-up in passing the port
parts.note: sounds like a delay passing the decanter at dinner, but means a ban on ships or trade leaving harbour

explanation.surface: Someone at the dinner table is slow to pass the port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' suggests the after-dinner wine; it is a harbour where trade is blocked by official order.
explanation.definitionFit: An official ban on trade or ships entering or leaving port holds up commerce.
